article: XXVII (no threshold invention — every operational threshold carries provenance, class, uncertainty, justification)
operator_directive: R420 section 5: record memory-threshold provenance — measurement environment, measurement date, observed baseline, safety margin rationale, threshold, intended execution context, uncertainty/limitations

measurement_environment.image: python:3.12-slim (Debian trixie 2026) + pinned Blender 5.2.1 LTS x64 (tarball sha256 a31f524fa99a527d3d52b7f5aaa68c34e1a19d5a1c9473f79c5cc610fd5b10e9, verified at image build)
measurement_environment.method: resident set size of the blender subprocess observed while authoring the R419c guard; order-of-magnitude figure, not a distribution

uncertainty: single-point observation, not a sampled distribution; scene geometry, Cycles render buffers, and denoising add unmeasured per-scene overhead on top (bridge scenes observed adding on the order of tens to a few hundred MB)
RSS is measured at one moment; peak during tile rendering can be higher
the measurement was taken by the implementing agent inside the container (AI_REVIEW provenance, Art. LXVII) — not an independent instrumented benchmark

measurements.quantity: full-quality hero+section+exploded bundle wall time (pinned build, local verification host)
measurements.observed_value: ~208 s total (hero 65-67 s, section 67-68 s, exploded 74-75 s)
rounds: R419 render-pipeline test runs (two independent runs: 207.59 s and 208.51 s)

measurement_environment.host: local verification container (faster CPU than the free-tier shared core)
measurement_environment.parameters: Cycles CPU, 48 samples, adaptive threshold 0.02, denoising on, 1152x768, three views

uncertainty: two runs, same host — no cross-host distribution

the deployed free-tier shared CPU is materially slower: the live production run ts_c0f41af92195 exceeded the full 900 s bundle budget on 2026-09-07 (BRIDGE_REPORT.json: RENDER_TIMEOUT), which is the direct evidence the async quality ladder exists

thresholds.name: in_worker memory guard
thresholds.intended_execution_context: the bridge RENDER step inside the discovery-run worker (the gauntlet worker process still resident)
thresholds.safety_margin_rationale: observed Blender baseline 269 MB + per-scene geometry/Cycles buffers (unmeasured, assumed up to roughly 2x baseline on bridge scenes) + the run worker's own residency on the same instance; the threshold is deliberately conservative because an OOM kill in-worker kills the RUN itself, converting a presentation skip into a user-visible run failure (Art. LXI inversion)
thresholds.justification_for_not_another_number: 650 MB gives ~2.4x the measured baseline; lowering it toward the baseline risks worker deaths on the only instance class observed (512 MB free tier, MemAvailable inflated by reclaimable cache); raising it further would make the guard never fire, silently returning to the pre-R419c OOM regime

thresholds.name: async memory guard
thresholds.intended_execution_context: the detached artifact-render job (the run worker has exited; its memory is freed)
thresholds.safety_margin_rationale: Blender baseline 269 MB + scene/buffer headroom with the run worker gone; ~1.5x baseline. The job may be killed by OOM without any user-visible run damage (it is a detached presentation job with a typed record), so the margin can be tighter than in_worker
thresholds.justification_for_not_another_number: below ~1.5x baseline the job would OOM during tile rendering on scenes only marginally above the trivial baseline; above it, the free-tier instance (MemAvailable typically < 500 MB after boot) would never start the job at all, making the async path dead code on the only instance class that needs it

thresholds.name: in_worker render budget
thresholds.intended_execution_context: the bridge RENDER step inside the discovery-run worker; env-overridable via ENGINE_RENDER_INWORKER_TIMEOUT_S (minimum 60)
thresholds.safety_margin_rationale: local full-quality bundle is ~208 s; 300 s lets a capable instance complete full quality in-worker, while a slow instance hands off to the async job after 5 minutes instead of the pre-R420 900 s hostage situation (observed live: ts_c0f41af92195 spent the whole 900 s budget and produced nothing)
thresholds.justification_for_not_another_number: 208 s local + ~45% headroom covers capable instances; anything longer re-creates the observed run-hostage defect; anything shorter hands off even on capable instances and wastes the in-worker attempt

thresholds.name: async render budget (attempt 1, full quality)
thresholds.safety_margin_rationale: the full bundle budget from R419; the async job has no user waiting on the same request, so it can afford the long attempt before the ladder degrades
thresholds.justification_for_not_another_number: the deployed instance exceeded 900 s at full quality (observed); the ladder therefore degrades quality rather than extending time indefinitely — presentation quality is the tunable, never the truth

thresholds.name: async quality ladder attempts 2-3
thresholds.value: attempt 2: 16 samples, 960x640, 420 s; attempt 3: 6 samples, 768x512, 240 s
thresholds.intended_execution_context: async artifact-render job retries after a timed-out/failed higher-quality attempt
thresholds.safety_margin_rationale: render cost scales ~linearly with sample count and ~quadratically with pixel count; 48->16->6 samples with the matching resolution steps moves the deployed-instance cost from >900 s into the hundreds-of-seconds regime while keeping a presentable studio image; bounded at three attempts so the job is always terminal-honest (no infinite retry loop)
thresholds.justification_for_not_another_number: three rungs span a ~13x compute reduction; fewer rungs leave a gap between full quality and the free-tier capacity, more rungs extend wall time past the value of a slightly better PNG
thresholds.disclosure: the achieved samples/resolution are recorded in render_record.json and projected into the CIO renders block — a degraded-quality render is DISCLOSED, never silently passed off as full quality

cross_cutting.threshold_class_discipline: all thresholds above are ENGINEERING (infrastructure capacity), never SCIENTIFIC — a render skip changes no epistemic state (Art. LXI); conceptual geometry is never promoted by a successful render (Art. XXVIII)
intended_execution_contexts: Render free-tier 512 MB container (the deployed production instance)
local verification hosts (BLENDER_PATH pointing at the same pinned 5.2.1 LTS build)
limitations: MemAvailable (from /proc/meminfo) includes reclaimable page cache; it is a proxy for launchability, not a hard reservation
the free-tier container shares its host CPU; render wall time varies with neighbor load, which the time budgets absorb only statistically

thresholds are calibrated against ONE deployed instance class and one local host; a plan upgrade (owner-gated, Art. LXV) changes the memory calculus and this record should be revised with new measurements then
no automated CI measurement re-derives these numbers; revision requires a new dated entry appended here (never silent drift, Art. XXVII)
sources: live BRIDGE_REPORT.json of run ts_c0f41af92195 (RENDER_TIMEOUT at 900 s, 2026-09-07, deployed R419f engine)
local pinned-build bundle timings 207.59 s / 208.51 s (R419 test artifacts)
R419c/R419f guard authoring measurements (269 MB baseline)

revision_history.change: the measurement BASIS of every memory guard changed: _mem_available_mb now reads the CONTAINER's cgroup headroom (memory.max - memory.current, cgroup v2; limit/usage_in_bytes, v1) and returns the MINIMUM of cgroup headroom and host /proc/meminfo MemAvailable. /proc/meminfo inside the container reports the HOST — on the Render Starter plan (512 MB cgroup, buildPlan verified via the Render API) the R419f-era guard read GBs of host availability, passed, and launched Blender into over-subscription; the cgroup OOM killer crashed the container (observed live 2026-09-07: boots at 23:04 and 23:40 in the runtime-state branch, each fresh-disk restart resetting run progress). The threshold VALUES are unchanged; what changed is that they are now measured against the real limit. On the 512 MB plan the honest outcome is a typed RENDER_SKIPPED_LOW_MEMORY with the owner-gated plan-upgrade note (Art. LXV) — the guard now performs the protection it always claimed.
revision_history.record_basis_note: guard records now carry mem_available_basis (CGROUP / HOST / CGROUP_AND_HOST)
